title: feat(agents): support custom provider brand-marks via record paths and user assets
head: 290b9d9841b0
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: User asset added after initial failed lookup is never retried
leads.consequence: For a custom provider with no existing SVG, the Image walks past the missing user file, ends with source empty and displays the glyph. Adding ~/.config/omarchy/agents/assets/<id>.svg afterward leaves candidatesKey identical; neither the asset nor refreshed record is watched for candidate URL changes. Image.source stays empty, so the user must switch to another provider and back (or restart the shell) before the newly installed mark can appear. A record refresh with identical URLs is not enough. Suggested change: watch the user asset path or explicitly reset/retry the candidate walker on a refresh/open when the current candidates failed.
leads.triage: behavioural; Opus follow-up (opus/followup-runtime-mark.md) confirmed runtime-added marks not retried (same reset rules as pre-PR) -> optional note; follow-up also found new F4 walker regression, published as lead finding

leads.summary: Light-only record icon is dropped by the outer icon guard
leads.consequence: A usage record with iconLight set but icon omitted or empty shows neither the provided mark nor an error on light surfaces. The field is copied by displayProvider but Panel only enters the iconLight branch when p.icon is truthy; the bundled/user fallbacks and then glyph win. Suggested change: test iconLight independently on light surfaces before optional icon, preserving fallback order. Synthetic headless function run shows the light-only URL is absent (reproducers/only-icon-light.md).
leads.triage: corroborates Opus N1 (iconLight alone ignored); published as optional note

leads.summary: User asset cannot override an existing packaged brand mark
leads.consequence: For claude, codex (both surfaces) and fireworks, a nonempty packaged SVG precedes ~/.config/omarchy/agents/assets/<id>.svg, so a user mark for the same id is never reached if the bundled SVG loads. If open PR #12352 merges, its newly bundled grok.svg and grok-light.svg produce the same outcome for grok. Explicit record.icon can override. This is relevant if the user-assets location is intended to customize existing providers rather than only new IDs; reverse user/bundled priority or document the limitation. Synthetic headless candidate order is in reproducers/user-assets-bundled-precedence.md.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus N3 (built-in precedes user marks); #12352 grok assets verified with gh; published as optional note

leads.summary: Literal file URLs break for icon paths containing # or ?
leads.consequence: A valid absolute icon file such as /example/home/a#b.svg is converted to file:///example/home/a#b.svg. Qt parses #b.svg as URL fragment (and ? as query) instead of a path segment, so the file never loads and the panel falls back to another mark or glyph. The same issue affects user assets when HOME/XDG_CONFIG_HOME has these characters or a provider ID includes them. The repository already provides Util.fileUrl(path) with path-segment encoding. Use it, or QUrl.fromLocalFile equivalent, for filesystem paths. Synthetic headless candidate URL in reproducers/unescaped-file-path.md, Qt source confirms delimiter handling.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus F2 (unencoded file URLs); published

leads.summary: Relative record icon resolves in the built-in panel, not next to its collector
leads.consequence: A third-party collector writing icon: 'assets/myagent.svg' as a relative path to its own plugin directory cannot load that file: Qt.resolvedUrl resolves it relative to the calling Panel.qml under the installed shell. A common icon: '~/brand.svg' is likewise sought under shell/plugins/agents/~/brand.svg, not HOME. Absolute filesystem paths work unless their URL bytes need encoding. Either expand ~/$HOME, define a secure collector-relative base (the panel has no collector path), or document that icon fields must contain an absolute file path or a URL. Synthetic headless tilde candidate in reproducers/relative-record-icon.md.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus F1 (relative/tilde paths panel-relative); published

leads.summary: Synced-only provider drops its record icon metadata
leads.consequence: When a provider has usage only on another device, aggregateSnapshots creates its stats but does not copy icon or iconLight to the snapshot; enabledProviders synthesizes displayProvider({id,name}), and the new display fields become empty. The tab can only use a locally installed user asset or a bundled mark; a custom record icon on the originating device alone never reaches the other device's panel. If remote-only tabs should retain marks, carry a safe portable icon identifier or require/install a user asset on each machine and document that limitation. Not reproduced in live QML, confirmed by the producer and consumer source.
leads.triage: covered by Opus (synced-only providers fall back; snapshots carry no icon); not a defect; not published

leads.summary: Added panel tests do not exercise the icon-resolution code
leads.consequence: The four new regex assertions pass even if none of the record icon or user-asset URLs is added to the candidate array. In a disposable sandbox copy, a mutant that replaces each new candidate push with void(...) passes all ten assertions. Add value assertions evaluating iconCandidatesForProvider with fake Qt/Quickshell (as the neighboring agent-usage-claude-limits-test.sh already extracts Panel functions), and include light-only, XDG home, ordering and bad-record fallback cases. Actual mutant run in reproducers/weak-panel-test.md.

limits: No Wayland compositor or GPU allocated, Qt GUI Image rendering not executed; candidate functions were run headlessly with explicit Qt/Quickshell stubs, and runtime-specific Image behavior was traced in upstream source.

Public open-PR searches returned many older, unrelated feature PRs; targeted shared-file and collector PRs were inspected, but the search universe was not exhaustively merged or tested. The cross-PR grok consequence is a source-confirmed candidate-order effect, not an actual dual-PR build run.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** The mark walker can skip a loaded mark after a light/dark or provider switch.

### Walker skips a found mark

On a list change, `source` first loads the old index; if that fails, its queued `candidateIndex++` runs after the reset and skips the loaded mark. **Impact:** a light-to-dark switch drops Claude's or Fireworks' built-in mark until the tab changes, and some provider switches drop record or user marks (headless Qt 6.11.2 walker copy).

**Suggested change:** advance only if `source` still equals the failed URL.

<details><summary>Reproducer (standalone walker copy, Qt 6.11.2)</summary>

Reviewed head: 290b9d9841b06110ce771af15100aae7380b63ac (omacom/omarchy PR #11896). The walker lines are unchanged by the PR (`shell/plugins/agents/Panel.qml` 437-460 at head); what changes is the length of the candidate lists it walks.

`walker-list-change.qml` copies the walker and shows a provider whose only mark is `assets/claude.svg` (like Claude and Fireworks, which have no `-light` twin), first on a light surface and then on a dark one, as a live theme switch does. Walker `pr` gets the lists the PR builds (built-in candidates, then the user assets directory, which is empty here). Walker `before` gets the lists the panel built before the PR.

Run in a directory that contains `assets/claude.svg` (the recorded run used `<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="16" height="16"><rect width="16" height="16" fill="#e0442a"/></svg>`) and nothing else. Recorded command, Qt 6.11.2: `QT_FORCE_STDERR_LOGGING=1 QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen QT_QUICK_BACKEND=software QT_LOGGING_RULES="qt.qpa.*=false" qml walker-list-change.qml`.

```qml
import QtQuick

// Standalone copy of the agents panel's hero-mark fallback walker (Panel.qml).
// Both walkers show a provider whose only mark is assets/claude.svg (no -light
// twin, like Claude and Fireworks), first on a light surface, then on a dark
// one, as a live theme switch does. `pr` uses the candidate lists PR #11896
// builds (built-in, then the user assets directory); `before` uses the lists
// the panel built before the PR. Run next to assets/claude.svg with:
//   QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen qml walker-list-change.qml
Item {
  id: root
  width: 64
  height: 64

  property bool light: true

  component Walker: Item {
    id: heroMark
    property bool light: true
    property var lightCandidates: []
    property var darkCandidates: []
    property var candidates: light ? lightCandidates : darkCandidates
    property string candidatesKey: candidates.join("\n")
    property int candidateIndex: 0
    onCandidatesKeyChanged: candidateIndex = 0
    property alias status: heroMarkImage.status
    property alias source: heroMarkImage.source
    width: 32
    height: 32

    Image {
      id: heroMarkImage
      anchors.fill: parent
      source: heroMark.candidateIndex < heroMark.candidates.length ? heroMark.candidates[heroMark.candidateIndex] : ""
      onStatusChanged: if (status === Image.Error && heroMark.candidateIndex < heroMark.candidates.length)
        Qt.callLater(function() { heroMark.candidateIndex++ })
    }
  }

  Walker {
    id: pr
    light: root.light
    lightCandidates: [Qt.resolvedUrl("assets/claude-light.svg"), Qt.resolvedUrl("assets/claude.svg"),
      Qt.resolvedUrl("user-assets/claude-light.svg"), Qt.resolvedUrl("user-assets/claude.svg")]
    darkCandidates: [Qt.resolvedUrl("assets/claude.svg"), Qt.resolvedUrl("user-assets/claude.svg")]
  }

  Walker {
    id: before
    light: root.light
    lightCandidates: [Qt.resolvedUrl("assets/claude-light.svg"), Qt.resolvedUrl("assets/claude.svg")]
    darkCandidates: [Qt.resolvedUrl("assets/claude.svg")]
  }

  function describe(name, w) {
    var source = String(w.source)
    return name + ": index " + w.candidateIndex + " of " + w.candidates.length
      + ", status " + ["Null", "Ready", "Loading", "Error"][w.status]
      + ", showing " + (source === "" ? "nothing (glyph)" : source.split("/").slice(-2).join("/"))
  }

  // Local files load synchronously; move on once nothing has changed for 20 ticks.
  property int stable: 0
  property string last: ""
  Timer {
    interval: 20
    repeat: true
    running: true
    onTriggered: {
      var now = root.describe("pr", pr) + " | " + root.describe("before", before)
      root.stable = now === root.last ? root.stable + 1 : 0
      root.last = now
      if (root.stable < 20) return
      console.log((root.light ? "light surface" : "after switching to a dark surface"))
      console.log("  " + root.describe("pr", pr))
      console.log("  " + root.describe("before", before))
      if (root.light) {
        root.light = false
        root.stable = 0
      } else {
        Qt.quit()
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## Actual output (exit 0; stdout was empty, this is stderr)

The run directory prefix is shown as `<workdir>/`; nothing else in the output is changed.

```
file://<workdir>/walker-list-change.qml:31:5: QML Image: Cannot open: file://<workdir>/assets/claude-light.svg
file://<workdir>/walker-list-change.qml:31:5: QML Image: Cannot open: file://<workdir>/assets/claude-light.svg
qml: light surface
qml:   pr: index 1 of 4, status Ready, showing assets/claude.svg
qml:   before: index 1 of 2, status Ready, showing assets/claude.svg
file://<workdir>/walker-list-change.qml:31:5: QML Image: Cannot open: file://<workdir>/user-assets/claude.svg
file://<workdir>/walker-list-change.qml:31:5: QML Image: Cannot open: file://<workdir>/user-assets/claude.svg
qml: after switching to a dark surface
qml:   pr: index 2 of 2, status Null, showing nothing (glyph)
qml:   before: index 0 of 1, status Ready, showing assets/claude.svg
```

On the light surface both walkers show `assets/claude.svg` at index 1. After the switch, `before` shows it at index 0 of the one-entry dark list, while `pr` ends at index 2 of 2 with nothing loaded, so the panel would show the bar glyph.

Why: when `candidates` changes, the `source` binding is evaluated with the old index (1) against the new list and loads `user-assets/claude.svg`, which fails and queues `candidateIndex++`. `onCandidatesKeyChanged` then resets the index to 0 and `assets/claude.svg` loads, but the queued increment still runs and moves the walk past it. Before the PR the dark list had one entry, so the old index 1 was out of range, `source` became empty, and nothing was queued. The two `Cannot open ... user-assets/claude.svg` lines are the stale load and the extra step.
</details>

### Relative record paths resolve in the panel directory

`toUrl()` resolves non-absolute paths against the root-owned `Panel.qml` directory. **Impact:** `~/...` and plugin-relative icons never load; for third-party ids, `assets/<id>.svg` repeats a built-in URL and stalls the dark-surface walk.

**Suggested change:** accept only absolute paths and `file://` URLs, and document it.

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at 290b9d98)</summary>

Reviewed head: 290b9d9841b06110ce771af15100aae7380b63ac (omacom/omarchy PR #11896).

## Test (PR's own style)

Save as `test/shell.d/agents-panel-icon-paths-test.sh` in a checkout of the reviewed head and run `bash test/shell.d/agents-panel-icon-paths-test.sh`. It slices the real `iconCandidatesForProvider()` out of `Panel.qml` and evaluates it, the same way `test/shell.d/agent-usage-claude-limits-test.sh` evaluates the limit helpers. `Qt.resolvedUrl()` is stubbed with standard URL resolution against the panel's install URL; on Qt 6.11.2 the real `Qt.resolvedUrl()` returned the same strings as this stub for equivalent inputs (a `~/` path, `assets/zai.svg`, and a relative file name).

```bash
#!/bin/bash

set -euo pipefail

source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"

# Evaluates the panel's mark candidates the way agent-usage-claude-limits-test.sh
# evaluates the limit helpers. Qt.resolvedUrl() resolves a relative string
# against the QML file that calls it, so the stub resolves against Panel.qml's
# install location.
run_node_test <<'JS'
const fs = require('fs')
const panel = fs.readFileSync(root + '/shell/plugins/agents/Panel.qml', 'utf8')
const start = panel.indexOf('function colorChannelLuminance')
const end = panel.indexOf('// Nothing to report, nothing in the bar')
assert(start > 0 && end > start, 'agents panel exposes its mark helpers')

const panelUrl = 'file:///usr/share/omarchy/shell/plugins/agents/Panel.qml'
const Qt = { resolvedUrl: (url) => new URL(String(url), panelUrl).href }
const Quickshell = { env: (name) => ({ HOME: '/home/me' })[name] || null }
const Color = { background: { r: 0.1, g: 0.1, b: 0.15 } }
const utilSource = fs.readFileSync(root + '/shell/Commons/Util.qml', 'utf8')
const Util = new Function(utilSource.slice(utilSource.indexOf('function fileUrl(path)'), utilSource.indexOf('function isVideoPath')) + '\nreturn { fileUrl }')()
eval(panel.slice(start, end))

const dark = { r: 0.1, g: 0.1, b: 0.15 }
for (const icon of ['~/.local/share/zai/zai.svg', 'icons/zai.svg', 'assets/zai.svg']) {
  const candidates = iconCandidatesForProvider({ providerId: 'zai', icon: icon, iconLight: '' }, dark).map(String)
  console.log(`icon ${JSON.stringify(icon)} -> ${JSON.stringify(candidates, null, 2)}`)
}

for (const icon of ['~/.local/share/zai/zai.svg', 'icons/zai.svg']) {
  const candidates = iconCandidatesForProvider({ providerId: 'zai', icon: icon, iconLight: '' }, dark).map(String)
  const insidePanel = new URL(icon, panelUrl).href
  assert(!candidates.includes(insidePanel), `record icon ${icon} is not looked up inside the panel's own directory`, `unexpected candidate: ${insidePanel}`)
}

// The hero walker cannot step past a URL equal to the one that just failed.
const repeated = iconCandidatesForProvider({ providerId: 'zai', icon: 'assets/zai.svg', iconLight: '' }, dark).map(String)
assertEqual(new Set(repeated).size, repeated.length, 'record icon assets/zai.svg does not repeat a built-in candidate')
JS
```

## Why a repeated URL matters: standalone walker copy on Qt 6.11.2

`walker-repeat.qml` copies the hero-mark fallback walker from `Panel.qml` and feeds it two lists that end in an existing `present.svg`: one with two different missing files first, one with the same missing file twice. Run in a directory that contains `present.svg` (the recorded run used `<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="16" height="16"><rect width="16" height="16" fill="#e0442a"/></svg>`). Recorded command: `QT_FORCE_STDERR_LOGGING=1 QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen QT_QUICK_BACKEND=software QT_LOGGING_RULES="qt.qpa.*=false" qml walker-repeat.qml` (Qt 6.11.2).

```qml
import QtQuick

// Standalone copy of the agents panel's hero-mark fallback walker (Panel.qml),
// fed two candidate lists. Run next to a present.svg with:
//   QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen qml walker-repeat.qml
Item {
  id: root
  width: 64
  height: 64

  component Walker: Item {
    id: heroMark
    property var candidates: []
    property string candidatesKey: candidates.join("\n")
    property int candidateIndex: 0
    onCandidatesKeyChanged: candidateIndex = 0
    property alias status: heroMarkImage.status
    width: 32
    height: 32

    Image {
      id: heroMarkImage
      anchors.fill: parent
      source: heroMark.candidateIndex < heroMark.candidates.length ? heroMark.candidates[heroMark.candidateIndex] : ""
      onStatusChanged: if (status === Image.Error && heroMark.candidateIndex < heroMark.candidates.length)
        Qt.callLater(function() { heroMark.candidateIndex++ })
    }
  }

  // Distinct missing URLs, then a present one.
  Walker {
    id: distinct
    candidates: [Qt.resolvedUrl("missing-a.svg"), Qt.resolvedUrl("missing-b.svg"), Qt.resolvedUrl("present.svg")]
  }

  // The same missing URL twice in a row, then a present one.
  Walker {
    id: repeated
    candidates: [Qt.resolvedUrl("missing-a.svg"), Qt.resolvedUrl("missing-a.svg"), Qt.resolvedUrl("present.svg")]
  }

  function describe(name, w) {
    return name + ": index " + w.candidateIndex + " of " + w.candidates.length
      + ", status " + ["Null", "Ready", "Loading", "Error"][w.status]
  }

  // Local files load synchronously; report once neither walker has moved for 20 ticks.
  property int stable: 0
  property string last: ""
  Timer {
    interval: 20
    repeat: true
    running: true
    onTriggered: {
      var now = root.describe("distinct", distinct) + " | " + root.describe("repeated", repeated)
      root.stable = now === root.last ? root.stable + 1 : 0
      root.last = now
      if (root.stable >= 20) {
        console.log(root.describe("distinct", distinct))
        console.log(root.describe("repeated", repeated))
        Qt.quit()
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Actual output (exit 0; stdout was empty, this is stderr):

The run directory prefix is shown as `<workdir>/`; nothing else in the output is changed.

```
file://<workdir>/walker-repeat.qml:21:5: QML Image: Cannot open: file://<workdir>/missing-a.svg
file://<workdir>/walker-repeat.qml:21:5: QML Image: Cannot open: file://<workdir>/missing-a.svg
file://<workdir>/walker-repeat.qml:21:5: QML Image: Cannot open: file://<workdir>/missing-b.svg
qml: distinct: index 2 of 3, status Ready
qml: repeated: index 1 of 3, status Error
```

With two different missing files the walk reaches `present.svg`. With the same missing URL twice it stops at index 1 in `Error`, because `Image` ignores a `source` that equals the current one (`QQuickImageBase::setSource()` returns early when `url == d->url`), so no second `statusChanged` fires. In the panel this means a record with `"icon": "assets/zai.svg"` on a dark surface never reaches `~/.config/omarchy/agents/assets/zai.svg`, even when that file exists.

<details><summary>More findings: file URLs, test assertions</summary>

### File URLs are built without encoding

`toUrl()` and the user-directory candidates use `"file://" + path`, and any string containing `://` is passed through. **Impact:** a `#` in an absolute path moves the rest into the URL fragment and the mark does not load, and an `https://` icon makes the panel request it over the network.

**Suggested change:** build these URLs with `Util.fileUrl()`, as `iconSource()` in `NotificationCard.qml` does, and pass through only `file://` (and `image://` if theme icons are wanted).

### The new test assertions only match source text

The four new checks look for strings in `Main.qml` and `Panel.qml`. **Impact:** the merge-base code plus two comments containing those strings passes all 10 checks, as do mutants that delete the new record or user-directory candidates or reorder them.

**Suggested change:** slice and evaluate `iconCandidatesForProvider()` the way `agent-usage-claude-limits-test.sh` evaluates the limit helpers, and assert the candidate lists for light and dark surfaces, record icons and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` set or unset.
</details>

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Verified** (headless Qt 6.11.2 probe of the real function and walker on a fresh walk, and sandbox test runs):
- An existing absolute record `icon` loads first; `iconLight` is tried first on light surfaces.
- User-directory marks in `~/.config/omarchy/agents/assets/` load on light and dark surfaces, including the `-light` twin; with `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` set, the candidates move to `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/omarchy/agents/assets/` (checked as candidate strings).
- A missing record icon falls through to the built-in and user-directory candidates.
- The PR test passes 10/10 at head and the patch applies cleanly to current `quattro` with the same result; the neighbouring agent usage tests pass.

**Optional notes:**
- `iconLight` without `icon` is ignored, because the whole record branch is gated on `p.icon`; either document that or accept `iconLight` alone.
- A mark added to the user directory while the shell runs is not picked up by refreshes or by reopening the panel; nothing watches the directory, so it appears after switching tabs away and back, a light/dark change or a restart. A README sentence would avoid confusion.
- Precedence is record, then built-in, then user directory, so a user mark cannot replace a bundled one (for example Grok's, if #12352 lands); the README states neither this nor the `-light` twin in the user directory.
